items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: my bass player at that time was a guy named Harry Grey

ctx.x: Until this union started in Chicago, and then we went down to five. My -- of course, my bass player at that time was a guy named Harry Grey who later became the President of the Musicians' Local in Chicago. There was two locals at that time -- local 10 and our local in Chicago. And Harry Grey was the President -- he didn't want to run, we had to make him run for office. And he won by a landslide. So, he was quite a guy. So he was the one that got us a five-day week deal with seven-day pay, you know.
